cases.sense: the direct object; the destination of motion
possession: a relation between two nouns, not to the verb

cases.note: Pāṇini counts only seven cases: the vocative is the nominative used for address, so it is named, not numbered, and its dual and plural are identical to the nominative's.

uses.description: Subject of an active verb
uses.question: The subject (the doer) of an active verb

uses.description: Subjective complement: a noun linked to the subject by “be” or “become”; both words take the same case
uses.question: A noun linked to the subject by “be” or “become” (“Rāma is king”)

uses.description: A noun in apposition to the subject (a second noun naming the same person)
uses.question: A noun in apposition to the subject (“Rāma, the hero, conquers”)

uses.description: An adjective modifying a noun in the nominative (adjectives take the case of their noun)
uses.question: An adjective describing the subject (“the beautiful boy comes”)

uses.description: The neuter nominative singular can work as an indeclinable adverb: सुखम् “happily”
uses.question: Which case, in the neuter singular, can work as an indeclinable adverb (सुखम् “happily”)?

uses.description: Direct object of a transitive verb (the thing acted upon)
uses.question: The direct object of a transitive verb (the thing acted upon)

uses.description: Objective complement: a noun linked to the direct object by an implied “be” or “become”
uses.question: A noun linked to the direct object by an implied “be” (“we know Rāma to be a hero”)

uses.description: Destination of a verb of motion
uses.question: The destination of a verb of motion (“goes to the forest”)

uses.description: Occasionally, with some prepositions (above, below, near, around, towards…)
uses.question: Which case do some prepositions meaning “above, below, near, around” occasionally take?

uses.description: The instrument used in the action
uses.question: The instrument used in an action (“kills with an arrow”)

uses.description: The agent (doer) of a passive verb or passive participle
uses.question: The agent (doer) of a passive verb or passive participle (“killed by the king”)

uses.description: Accompaniment, usually with सह, समम् or साकम् (“with”), which can also be left out
uses.question: Accompaniment, “with”, usually alongside सह, समम् or साकम्

uses.description: विना (“without”) usually takes the instrumental (sometimes the dative, 4f)
uses.question: Which case does विना (“without”) usually take?

uses.description: Cause or reason (हेतु): “because of, owing to” (the ablative can also express cause, 5c)
uses.question: Cause or reason (हेतु): “by, owing to” (“the jīva is bound by sorrow”)

uses.description: With सदृश and तुल्य (“equal to, same as”)
uses.question: Which case do सदृश and तुल्य (“equal to, same as”) take?

uses.description: An instrumental noun can be used adverbially: सुखेन “happily”
uses.question: Besides the neuter nominative (सुखम्), which case of a noun can serve as an adverb (“happily”)?

uses.description: In expressions like “by name”, “by nature”
uses.question: Expressions like “by name” or “by nature”

uses.description: With अलम् and कृतम् (“enough!”): अलं दुःखेन “enough with sorrow”
uses.question: Which case do अलम् and कृतम् (“enough with…!”) take?

uses.description: किम् + a noun in the instrumental = “what is the use of …?”
uses.question: किम् + which case of a noun means “what is the use of …?”

uses.description: Indirect object of verbs like “give, send, show”: the one to or for whom the action is done
uses.question: The indirect object of verbs like “give, send, show” (“gives the books to the students”)

uses.description: The person or thing for whose advantage the action is done (“for the sake of”)
uses.question: The person or thing for whose benefit the action is done (“rules for the sake of the people”)

uses.description: The purpose of an action
uses.question: The purpose of an action (“goes for war”)

uses.description: The object of verbs showing malice or anger
uses.question: The object of verbs of anger or malice (“angry with the son”)

uses.description: With the particles of reverence नमः and स्वस्ति
uses.question: Which case do the particles of reverence नमः and स्वस्ति take?

uses.description: विना (“without”) sometimes takes the dative (usually the instrumental, 3d)
uses.question: Besides its usual case, which case does विना (“without”) sometimes take?

uses.description: The place or time from which the action originates
uses.question: The place or time an action starts from (“goes from the forest”)

uses.description: The object of verbs meaning “to desist from”, “to protect (from)”, “to fear”
uses.question: The object of verbs meaning “desist from”, “protect from” or “fear”

uses.description: Cause or motive, “out of” (similar to the instrumental, 3e)
uses.question: Cause or motive: “out of” (“out of anger he strikes the boy”)

uses.description: With a comparative: the thing compared against (“other than”, “higher than”)
uses.question: The thing compared against, with a comparative (“other than”, “higher than”)

uses.description: With some prepositions (before, east of, after, until…)
uses.question: Which case do prepositions meaning “before, east of, after, until” take?

uses.description: Possession: the possessor is placed in the genitive, usually before the thing possessed
uses.question: The possessor (“Rāma's book”)

uses.description: Replaces the English verb “to have”: “Rāma has a wife” = “of Rāma there is a wife”
uses.question: Sanskrit has no verb “to have”: “Rāma has a wife” puts Rāma in which case?

uses.description: Sometimes used in place of the dative with verbs like “give”, “show”
uses.question: Which case sometimes replaces the dative with verbs like “give” or “show”?

uses.description: Often used in place of the dative to give the sense “for” (e.g. “qualified for”)
uses.question: Which case often replaces the dative for the sense “for” (“qualified for”)?

uses.description: The subject or object of an “-ing word” (a noun derived from a verb)
uses.question: The subject or object of an “-ing word”, a noun derived from a verb (“his grasping of the rope”)

uses.description: The place or time where the action takes place (in, at, on, upon, among)
uses.question: The place or time where an action takes place (“lives in the forest”)

uses.description: “With reference to”, “with regard to”, in terms of subject matter
uses.question: “With reference to, with regard to” a subject matter

uses.description: The object of love or devotion
uses.question: The object of love or devotion (“the king loves Rāma”)

uses.description: The absolute construction (सति सप्तमी), showing a simultaneous action
uses.question: The “absolute” construction (सति …), showing an action happening at the same time as the main one

uses.description: Direct address
uses.question: Directly addressing someone (“O Rāma!”)

examples.note: The angry man is the brahmin whose son Daśaratha has just shot.
The opening words of the reading. नाम “by name” is an indeclinable.

target.meaning: killed, dead (a participle used as an adjective)

examples.devanagari: सः अतीव धार्मिकः भूमिपः सुखं जीवति
examples.iast: saḥ atīva dhārmikaḥ bhūmipaḥ sukhaṃ jīvati
examples.note: सुखम् is the neuter singular, identical in the nominative and the accusative.
The verb's ending -मः carries the subject “we”.

examples.english: And he kills the [boy] with a sharp arrow.
examples.note: Daśaratha, hunting, shoots the brahmin's son, mistaking him for a deer.

examples.english: We know Rāma to be a [hero].
Rāma sees the pigeon as a [crow].
examples.note: Out of context it could equally be “sees the crow as a pigeon”: both nouns are accusative.
The last sentence of the reading: Daśaratha returns home under the brahmin's curse.

examples.english: One day a certain sage comes to [Ayodhyā].

examples.note: प्रति “towards” follows its accusative.

examples.devanagari: बालकः अपि सः वीरः बहून् राक्षसान् इषुभिः हन्ति
examples.iast: bālakaḥ api saḥ vīraḥ bahūn rākṣasān iṣubhiḥ hanti
examples.english: Though only a boy, that hero kills many rākṣasas with his [arrows].
The army of night-stalkers was struck down by [Rāma].
examples.note: From the Rāma prayer (रामो राजमणिः सदा विजयते…), memorized in class 26.

examples.devanagari: वयं मुनयः राक्षसैः अत्यन्तं पीडिताः भवामः
examples.iast: vayaṃ munayaḥ rākṣasaiḥ atyantaṃ pīḍitāḥ bhavāmaḥ
examples.english: We sages are terribly harassed by the [rākṣasas].
examples.note: The sage Viśvāmitra's complaint to Daśaratha.
सह can be left out: रामः सीतया गच्छति means the same.

examples.english: Rāma goes to the forest with the [sage].
I will marry [Sītā] (lit. make a marriage with Sītā).
examples.note: What every king thinks on hearing of Sītā. The present tense is used for an intended act.

examples.english: Rāma goes to the forest without [Sītā].

examples.note: The grieving brahmin, cursing Daśaratha.

examples.english: The jīva is bound by (owing to) [sorrow].
Because of your [misdeed] I suffer sorrow.
The teacher gives the books to the [students].
The king rules for (the sake of) the [people].
He goes for [war] (with the purpose of fighting).

examples.devanagari: ब्राह्मणैः सह सः प्रजायै यज्ञं करोति
examples.iast: brāhmaṇaiḥ saha saḥ prajāyai yajñaṃ karoti
examples.english: With the brahmins he performs a sacrifice for [offspring].
examples.note: Daśaratha, sonless, sacrifices for sons; four are born: Rāma, Lakṣmaṇa, Bharata and Śatrughna.

examples.english: Rāma comes for the [protection] of the sages from the rākṣasas.
examples.note: The same sentence shows 5b (राक्षसेभ्यः, protect from) and 6e (मुनीनां, object of the verbal noun रक्षण).

examples.english: The father is angry with the [son].

examples.note: From the Rāma prayer (रामो राजमणिः सदा विजयते…), memorized in class 26.

examples.english: Even the seers shrink in fear from the [rākṣasas].
examples.note: Simplified from the reading's relative clause येभ्यो राक्षसेभ्य ऋषयो ऽप्युद्विजन्ते “the rākṣasas from whom even the seers shrink”.

examples.english: Out of [anger] he strikes the boy.

examples.devanagari: त्वम् अपि अहम् इव पुत्रात् शोकम् अनुभवसि
examples.iast: tvam api aham iva putrāt śokam anubhavasi
examples.english: You too, like me, will suffer grief on account of a [son].
examples.note: The brahmin's curse on Daśaratha, fulfilled when Rāma is exiled.

examples.english: There is no higher refuge than [Rāma].
examples.note: From the Rāma prayer (रामो राजमणिः सदा विजयते…), memorized in class 26.
From the Rāma prayer (रामो राजमणिः सदा विजयते…), memorized in class 26.

examples.english: [Rāma] has a wife (of Rāma there is a wife).
The [king] has no sorrow (of the king there is no sorrow).
examples.note: What the people say of Daśaratha, before the curse.

examples.devanagari: जनकस्य अतीव रमणीया कन्या सीता नाम
examples.iast: janakasya atīva ramaṇīyā kanyā sītā nāma
examples.english: [Janaka] has a very lovely daughter named Sītā.
examples.note: No verb at all: “of Janaka (there is) a very lovely daughter”. अस्ति is understood.

examples.english: His grasping of the [rope] saved him.
examples.note: Both genitives hang on the verbal noun ग्रहणम् “grasping”: तस्य is its subject, रज्जोः its object.

examples.english: You alone are the protector of the [people].

target.meaning: subject (of a king); in the plural, the people

examples.note: रक्षकः “protector” is a noun made from the verb √रक्ष् “protect”, so what is protected goes in the genitive.

examples.english: In that [forest] lives a brahmin's son.
He lives happily in [Ayodhyā] with his wives.

examples.note: When the young Rāma draws his bow.

examples.english: A brahmin is a god among [men].

examples.devanagari: तस्मिन् देशे अतीव पण्डितः नृपः जनकः नाम राज्यं करोति
examples.iast: tasmin deśe atīva paṇḍitaḥ nṛpaḥ janakaḥ nāma rājyaṃ karoti
examples.english: In that [land] a very learned king named Janaka rules.
Who is capable of (with regard to) [killing] them?
examples.note: Daśaratha's question about the rākṣasas. तेषां is the object of the verbal noun हनन (6e).

examples.english: So the king loves [Rāma] above all.
May my mind always be absorbed in [Rāma].
examples.note: From the Rāma prayer (रामो राजमणिः सदा विजयते…), memorized in class 26.
The brahmin, to Daśaratha.
The last line of the Rāma prayer (रामो राजमणिः सदा विजयते…), memorized in class 26.
